R1 Deployment Field Notes

Unitree R1 · r1_ctrl · Deployment Q&A notes

Running a trained motion on the real R1: what happens, and what can go wrong

Notes from a follow-up discussion on stage 5 of the R1 motion-teaching workflow. Covers the run sequence after launching r1_ctrl, how the controller's modes relate to the factory software, failure cases, emergency stops, and how multiple motions fit together. Example motion throughout: R1 standing on one leg (Mimic_OneLeg).

The run sequence on the real robot

Steps 1–3 (hang the robot, L2 + R2 for debug mode, set PC IP 192.168.123.222/24) come first. These notes pick up from step 4.

4

Launch the controller

PC terminal · robot still fully hung
cd deploy/robots/r1/build
./r1_ctrl --network=enp5s0

What it is

  • r1_ctrl is the C++ program built with cmake .. && make, the same one used in sim2sim.
  • It reads joint angles and IMU from the robot and sends joint commands about 50 times per second, over DDS (unitree_sdk2).
  • --network names the PC's network interface wired to the robot. In sim2sim this was lo (loopback).
  • Run it from inside build/: config and policy paths are relative.

Finding the interface name

  1. Run ifconfig or ip a.
  2. Find the block with inet 192.168.123.222. Its name is the one to use.
  3. Onboard NIC: enp5s0, eno1. USB adapter: enx00e04c…. Never lo or wlp….
  4. ping the robot before launching. (.161 on G1; confirm the address for R1.)
Healthy start The program reports it is receiving robot state and sits in Passive. If it waits forever: wrong interface name, wrong IP, or debug mode not entered (factory software still holds the joints).
5

Step through the modes

Robot remote · r1_ctrl state machine

r1_ctrl is a finite state machine. Each mode runs its own controller; button combos from config.yaml switch between them.

ModeEnter withWhat the robot doesWhat you do
Passiveon start · LT + BJoints damped, limpRobot fully hung
FixStandLT + ↑Interpolates to the default standing pose over a few seconds, holds with PDWait until still, then lower the gantry: feet flat, carrying most of the weight, rope slightly slack
VelocityRT + AWalking policy runs, actively balancing. Left stick moves, right stick turnsSticks centred. Let it stand still a few seconds
Mimic_OneLegyour own combopolicy.onnx plays one_leg_left.npz from frame 0Hands off the sticks. Finger on LT + B

Where the entry combo goes

In Mimic_OneLeg, transitions: {Passive: LT + B.on_pressed} is the way out. The way in belongs in the Velocity state's transitions, e.g. Mimic_OneLeg: RB + X.on_pressed. Pick a combo that clashes with nothing. .on_pressed fires once per press.

Why go through Velocity

The motion starts from the default standing pose, and the policy only learned to start from there. Velocity hands it a robot that is balanced, still and in pose. Jumping in from FixStand or Passive risks a jolt or a fall on the first frame.

6

Motion ends, Velocity takes over

Automatic · end_state: Velocity

When playback passes the end of the .npz (10 s here), the state machine switches to Velocity by itself, so the walking policy catches the robot. FixStand would only hold joint angles stiffly and cannot rebalance a robot that is still swaying.

Run it again

Once standing still in Velocity, press the Mimic combo again.

Shut down

  1. Raise the gantry until the rope takes the weight.
  2. LT + B into Passive. The robot goes limp into the rope.
  3. Ctrl + C to stop r1_ctrl, then power off.

Questions that came up

Are Passive, FixStand and Velocity built into the robot?

Two brains, not one

  • Factory brain lives on the robot: stand, walk, the moves printed on the remote. L2 + R2 (debug mode) switches it off. It is not erased; a reboot brings it back.
  • Your brain is r1_ctrl on the PC. After debug mode, the robot only has low-level motor drivers. Every decision comes from r1_ctrl.
ModeKindSource
PassiveNo AI · dampingRepo C++ code
FixStandNo AI · PD to fixed poseRepo C++ code
VelocityRL policy (.onnx)Shipped in deploy/robots/r1
Mimic_OneLegRL policy (.onnx)You train and add it

Does the robot's own remote still work under r1_ctrl?

Yes, via a relay through the robot

Remote ──wireless──► R1 ──LAN / DDS──► PC: r1_ctrl
  • The robot packs button states into the state message it sends to the PC. r1_ctrl reads them. (This is how the G1 deploy works; confirm in the R1 code.)
  • Buttons now mean only what config.yaml says. The printed card on the remote no longer applies.
  • Cut the LAN and the remote is useless: presses reach the robot but not r1_ctrl. LT + B does nothing.
  • Sim2sim uses a USB gamepad on the PC instead. Re-test every combo on the real remote while the robot is fully hung.

What happens if r1_ctrl stops, hangs, or the LAN cable comes out?

The self-protection only covers half the cases

The "fall back to Passive" logic lives inside r1_ctrl. It needs the program alive and a working path for the Passive command to reach the robot.

Case 1 · program alive, detects the problem protected Mimic, second 4, on one leg. The policy loses it and the body tilts past the safety limit. r1_ctrl sees it on the IMU, switches to Passive, sends damping. The robot goes limp into the rope instead of fighting. Also covered: robot-to-PC data stops while PC-to-robot still works. r1_ctrl times out and sends Passive.
Case 2 · command path cut not protected A. Someone trips on the LAN cable. Passive is sent but has nowhere to go.
B. r1_ctrl crashes mid-motion. Nothing is left to detect or send.
C. The PC sleeps or a heavy app starves the control loop. What R1 does then depends on its low-level firmware (not confirmed): either holds the last command and topples like a statue, or drops torque and collapses. Either way, only the gantry saves it.

Mitigations

  • Find out R1's behaviour safely: fully hung, in FixStand, unplug the LAN and watch (stiff or limp).
  • Tie the cable to the gantry frame with enough slack; keep it out of walkways.
  • Disable PC sleep and screen lock; close browsers with many tabs and any running training job.

If the robot is still hung and I switch to Velocity, will it kick around?

Yes. Expected, not a bug

  • Velocity was only ever trained with feet on the ground, carrying the body.
  • Hung, the legs are unloaded and the body sways. The policy reads "falling" and does the one thing it learned: step. Stepping into air fixes nothing, so it keeps stepping.
  • Many walking policies also step in place even at zero command.
  • Mimic policies have the same problem.
Rule Use RL modes only with feet on the floor. Hung: Passive or FixStand. Lifting the robot at the end: go to FixStand or Passive before raising the gantry. If it is already kicking, LT + B immediately; don't lower it onto kicking legs.

Does the remote have an emergency stop that works in debug mode?

Three stop layers, very different reliability

1 · LT + B in r1_ctrlA mode switch defined in config.yaml. Needs r1_ctrl alive and the LAN connected. software
2 · Factory e-stopR1 manual: hold L2 + B for 5+ s. Belongs to the factory software, which debug mode turns off. Unverified there. test first
3 · Physical STOPBuilt-in STOP button on the upper-body panel, plus a GH1.25 external e-stop input. Works regardless of software. hardware

LT (repo docs) and L2 (manual) are most likely the same left trigger. Check in the manual whether STOP cuts motor power or damps; the robot drops either way.

Is every move on the remote a separate trained model that returns to Velocity afterwards?

For the factory moves: unknown. For your system: yes, by design

Factory moves (printed card)

The card lists Mode Switch items (standing, posture lock, damping/soft e-stop, running, stair climbing) and Customized Movements (stand up from lying, stretch, wave, dance…). Unitree does not publish how these are built. Commercial robots usually mix:

  • separate RL policies for whole-body moves (dance, getting up);
  • recorded joint trajectories for simple ones (arm wave over a balancing lower body);
  • variants of the locomotion controller (running, stairs).

Your r1_ctrl setup

Velocity ─combo A─► Mimic_OneLeg ─end─► Velocity
         ─combo B─► Mimic_Dance  ─end─► Velocity
         ─combo C─► Mimic_Wave   ─end─► Velocity
  • One Mimic state = one .onnx + one .npz + one entry combo.
  • end_state can chain into another motion if the poses match. Velocity is the safest hub.
  • One policy can learn a whole motion library, but it is harder to train. Start with one motion per model.
  • Keep your own button map; the remote has limited buttons.

Before every real-robot session

  • Whole button sequence rehearsed in sim2sim (--network=lo)
  • Gantry attached; robot fully hung at power-on
  • Debug mode entered (L2 + R2) before launching r1_ctrl
  • Correct interface name; robot answers ping
  • LAN cable tied to the frame with slack
  • PC sleep and screen lock off; heavy apps closed
  • Every combo re-tested on the real remote while hung
  • Physical STOP location known; behaviour on LAN loss known
  • Operator: remote, finger on LT + B
  • Spotter: beside the gantry, hand near STOP, ready to pull the rope
